subject: general
question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khilji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** was a prominent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who reigned from 1296 to 1316.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• Alauddin Khilji sent his trusted general, **Malik Kafur**, to lead expeditions to South India.
 
• Under Malik Kafur's command, the army successfully raided several kingdoms in the Deccan and South India, including the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, and Hoysalas.
 
• These expeditions were significant as they brought immense wealth to the Delhi Sultanate and expanded its influence to the southern regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Balban** was a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who focused more on consolidating power in the north rather than expanding southward.
 
• **Qutub-al-din Aibak** was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and laid the foundation for future rulers but did not engage in significant southern expeditions.
 
• **Iltutmish** was another significant ruler who consolidated the Sultanate's power in the north and built the administrative framework but did not send expeditions to South India.
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a series of dynasties that ruled northern India from the 13th to the 16th centuries, with significant contributions to Indian culture, architecture, and administration.
